name: Twig
waitingLines: Is {partner} coming back soon? Not that I’m waiting. I’m totally waiting. Nice weather.
Okay so I’ll just sit here quietly until {partner} gets home. Quietly. Mostly quietly.

questions.scene: Twig scurries in at top speed, hits your rug, slides, and pretends that was the plan.
lines: Hi hi hi okay so I was humming earlier and it made me think of a quiz. Nice weather.
questions.question: Male mice do something surprising to impress a mate. What is it?

choices.label: Bring her cheese
reply: Cute, very cartoon, but no.
Male mice sing ultrasonic love songs, way too high for humans to hear.
Real-life mice are basically secret boy bands.

choices.label: Sing high-pitched love songs
reply: YES. Mice sing! Ultrasonic serenades, too high for you to hear.
Male mice sing complex songs to court females.
If Sage could hear me sing... wait no, never mind. Nice weather.

choices.label: Do a little dance
reply: Okay, I would pay to see that.
They actually sing: ultrasonic songs humans can't hear.
Tiny love ballads happening in your walls right now. You're welcome.

questions.factBasis: Male mice produce ultrasonic courtship songs.

questions.scene: Twig unrolls a list titled '36 Questions' and immediately rolls it back up.
lines: This is research. For a friend. The friend is me.
questions.question: Psychologists created a set of 36 questions designed to do what?

choices.label: Help strangers feel close quickly
reply: Yes!! Strangers asking deep questions in turns!
The study found pairs felt surprisingly close afterward.
Should I ask Sage all 36? Is that too many? It's too many. Nice weather.

choices.label: Test if someone is lying
reply: No, that's a different, scarier test.
They're questions that help two people build closeness fast.
Taking turns opening up, a little more each round. So brave.

choices.label: Pick the perfect pizza topping
reply: I'd answer those instantly. Pineapple. Sorry.
It's a set designed to build closeness between strangers.
Questions get deeper slowly. Like my crush. Slowly. Deeper.

questions.factBasis: Aron et al. (1997) developed 36 questions to generate interpersonal closeness.

questions.scene: Twig touches a little potted plant and it folds its leaves shut. She gasps.
lines: IT'S SHY. IT'S LIKE ME.
questions.question: Why does the 'sensitive plant' (Mimosa) fold up when touched?

choices.label: It's allergic to fingers
reply: Haha! No.
It folds to protect itself, maybe to scare off hungry bugs.
Water rushes out of special cells, so the leaves collapse in seconds.

choices.label: It's falling asleep
reply: Aww, nap plant. Close, but no.
It's a defense move, triggered by touch.
Water shifts in its cells, so the leaves fold in seconds.

choices.label: A quick defense reaction
reply: Correct! A defense move!
Touch triggers water to rush out of cells, so leaves fold fast.
Same thing happens to me when Sage says hi. Instant fold.

questions.factBasis: Mimosa pudica folds leaves rapidly when touched, likely as defense.

questions.scene: Twig tilts her head left, then right, then left again, practicing something.
lines: Purely hypothetical tilting. Unrelated to any future plans.
questions.question: When people kiss, which way do most tilt their heads?

choices.label: To the left
reply: Some do! But most tilt right.
A study found about two-thirds of people tilt their heads right.
Lefties exist. They're the rebels of kissing.

choices.label: Straight on, no tilt
reply: Bonk. That's noses colliding.
Most people tilt right, about two out of three.
Straight on is how you headbutt. Romantically, maybe.

choices.label: To the right
reply: Yes! About two out of three people tilt right!
Scientists literally watched couples kissing in public to find this out.
Okay so I should tilt right. Noted. Not for anything. Nice weather.

questions.factBasis: Güntürkün (2003) observed ~2/3 of kissing couples turn heads to the right.

questions.scene: Twig picks up a smooth pebble from your garden and holds it like treasure.
lines: This is perfect. This is so perfect. For... no reason.
questions.question: What do gentoo penguins give potential mates?

choices.label: Small fish
reply: Snacks are romantic, but no.
Gentoo penguins give pebbles to their crushes.
Pebbles build their nests. It's literally a 'let's build a home' gift.

choices.label: Pebbles
reply: YES. Pebbles. I'm crying.
A good pebble helps build a nest, so it's a big deal.
Should I give Sage a pebble? Is that weird? Nice weather.

choices.label: Seashells
reply: Pretty, but no.
They give pebbles. Nest-building gifts.
A pebble from a penguin is basically a promise ring.

questions.factBasis: Gentoo penguins offer pebbles to mates during courtship.

questions.scene: Twig wraps her tail around a pen and lifts it, wobbling dramatically.
lines: Look look look. Okay I dropped it.
questions.question: What can a harvest mouse do with its tail?

choices.label: Grab onto grass stalks, like a fifth hand
reply: YES. A tail that grabs things!
Harvest mice wrap their tails around stems to climb and balance.
I tried. I dropped the pen. Still proud.

choices.label: Use it to send Morse code
reply: Ha! That would solve all my texting problems.
Harvest mice use their tails to grip grass stems while climbing.
Basically a fifth hand. Very handy. Sorry. Pun.

choices.label: Nothing, it's just decoration
reply: Rude to tails everywhere.
Harvest mice can grip grass stalks with their tails.
It helps them balance way up on wobbly stems.

questions.scene: Twig 'accidentally' walks past your window. Then again. Then again.
lines: Totally random. Very random. Science says this works, actually.
questions.question: What's the 'mere exposure effect'?

choices.label: You get sunburned if you stay outside
reply: That's just exposure. Mere sunburn.
It's about liking people and things more after seeing them often.
Familiar feels safe, and safe feels nice.

choices.label: We tend to like things more the more often we see them
reply: YES. Familiarity breeds fondness!
Repeated exposure tends to make things feel more likable.
This is why I walk past Sage's café daily. It's SCIENCE.

choices.label: Seeing something too much makes you hate it
reply: Sometimes! But usually the opposite.
Repeated exposure tends to increase liking.
Up to a point. I'll keep my walk-bys to twice a day.

questions.factBasis: Zajonc's mere-exposure effect: repeated exposure increases liking.

questions.scene: Twig arranges blue buttons on your table in a perfect line.
lines: Decorating! For a bird reason!
questions.question: How does a male bowerbird try to attract a mate?

choices.label: Builds and decorates a fancy display
reply: YES. Interior design for love!
Males build bowers and decorate with colorful objects, often blue ones.
Some even arrange items by size. Main character behavior.

choices.label: Sings opera
reply: Dramatic! Not the answer!
They build and decorate fancy structures called bowers.
Shiny objects, flowers, berries. Total aesthetic.

choices.label: Writes a love letter
reply: Okay, I'd faint.
They build a bower and decorate it with colorful treasures.
Blue is a favorite for some species. Taste.

questions.factBasis: Male bowerbirds build and decorate bowers to attract females.

questions.scene: Twig waves her arms and wiggles, doing a strange little dance.
lines: This is how spiders flirt. I've been practicing. Don't watch.
questions.question: How do male peacock spiders try to impress a mate?

choices.label: Bring her a fly with a bow on it
reply: Cute! Not real!
They lift a colorful flap on their abdomen and dance.
Tiny, colorful, bold. Everything I'm not.

choices.label: Spin a heart-shaped web
reply: Omg that would be adorable. No.
They show off a colorful flap and do a little dance.
Some are smaller than a grain of rice. Big moves, tiny body.

choices.label: Raise a colorful flap and dance
reply: YES!! A tiny rainbow dance!
They lift a bright, colorful fan and wave their legs in a dance.
If I danced for Sage, would he... no. Nice weather.

questions.factBasis: Male peacock spiders (Maratus) display colorful abdominal flaps and dance.

questions.scene: Twig turns to face the window, then turns to face you, then back again.
lines: I'm following the sun. And you. And the sun.
questions.question: What do young sunflowers do during the day?

choices.label: Stand completely still
reply: Nope! They move!
Young sunflowers turn to follow the sun across the sky.
Then they reset overnight. Like a crush reset.

choices.label: Follow the sun across the sky
reply: Correct! Sun-tracking babies!
Young sunflowers turn east to west, then reset overnight.
Grown-up flowers mostly face east. Committed. Respect.

choices.label: Close up like a book
reply: Aww, no.
Young sunflowers follow the sun all day.
Then they reset at night to face east again.

questions.factBasis: Young sunflowers track the sun (heliotropism); mature heads mostly face east.

questions.scene: Twig fans herself with a napkin. Her cheeks are very pink.
lines: Hypothetically, if someone, anyone, wanted to confess... Nice weather. Anyway.
questions.question: Confessing a crush: in person, or by text?

choices.label: In person
reply: In person?? With your actual face?? Legend.
I'd make eye contact for one second and then evaporate.

choices.label: By text
reply: By text. Safe. Editable. Smart.
You can rewrite it 40 times and nobody has to know. Not that I do that.

A:A: In person for both of you. A courage couple.
So you and {partner} looked each other in the eye and SAID it?
Okay I need a full replay. Slow motion. Please.
A:B: By text for you. {partner} wants it in person.
They want eye contact. You want the backspace key.
Text it, then show up with snacks. Best of both. Stealing this.
B:A: In person for you. {partner} would rather text it.
So you'd say it out loud, and they'd reply later with 'same' and a heart?
Honestly? That's my dream scenario. Writing it down.
B:B: By text for both of you. Typing champions.
I bet you and {partner} both stared at 'typing...' for ten full minutes.
That's my plan too. I have 14 drafts. It's fine.

questions.scene: Twig peeks around your door like she just happened to be passing by. For the third time.
lines: Total coincidence that I'm here. Total.
questions.question: Making the first move: ask them out directly, or 'accidentally' keep running into them?

choices.label: Ask directly
reply: Directly?! A hero walks among us.
No plan B, no hiding behind plants. Wow.

choices.label: 'Accidentally' run into them
reply: Strategic run-ins. My entire life strategy.
I know Sage's coffee schedule. For... unrelated reasons.

A:A: You both go direct. No games. Very healthy. Very scary.
Neither you nor {partner} would survive my method.
Can one of you write me a script? Bullet points are fine.
A:B: You'd plan the run-ins. {partner} would just ask.
You'd be hiding behind a plant while they walk up and say hi.
Let them do it. Accept graciously. Pretend you weren't hiding.
B:A: You'd ask directly. {partner} would rather 'run into' you.
So while they're memorizing your schedule, you just say 'coffee?'
Efficient. Brutal. Romantic. I'm taking notes.
B:B: Strategic run-ins for both of you. Masterminds.
Honestly, you and {partner} 'bumped into' each other for how many months?
I see you. I am you. Nice weather.

questions.scene: Twig clutches a tiny notebook full of crossed-out lines.
lines: Okay hypothetical gift for a hypothetical crush. Help. Fast.
questions.question: The perfect 'I like you' gift?

choices.label: A playlist
reply: A playlist. Every song is a secret clue.
Track seven says what you can't. Track eight says it louder.

choices.label: A handwritten note
reply: A handwritten note?! So brave.
Your handwriting is basically your heart, but in ink.

choices.label: Their favorite snack
reply: Their favorite snack. Sneaky and smart.
It says 'I pay attention to you.' Without saying it.

A:A: Playlist for both of you. Music nerds in love.
I can picture it: you and {partner} speak entirely in song lyrics.
Please tell me there's a shared playlist with a cheesy name.
A:B: Note for you. {partner} would rather get a playlist.
So they'd want feelings in song form, and you'd want them in ink.
Write the lyrics of their favorite song by hand. Combo achieved.
A:C: Snacks for you. {partner} prefers a playlist.
Snacks and songs. That's a whole date honestly.
Picnic, headphones, done. I'm so jealous.
B:A: Playlist for you. {partner} would rather get a note.
Easy fix: write one line for every song.
Track list with tiny love notes. I'm sweating. That's so good.
B:B: Handwritten notes for both of you. My heart.
I bet you and {partner} keep each other's notes in a box somewhere.
Don't answer. Just let me imagine it. Thank you.
B:C: Snacks for you. {partner} wants a handwritten note.
Write 'I like you' on the snack bag in marker.
Low effort, high impact. I'm writing this down. Wait. For no one.
C:A: Playlist for you. {partner} wants their favorite snack.
Make a playlist called 'songs to eat chips to.'
Gift both. Watch them crunch and smile.
C:B: Tape the note to their favorite snack. Romance AND protein.
They'll read it mid-bite. Perfect timing.
C:C: Favorite snack for both of you. Practical lovers.
Pretty sure you and {partner} show affection by knowing each other's chip flavor.
That's real intimacy. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise.

questions.scene: Twig's phone buzzes. Her group chat is named 'SAGE WATCH 2026'. She flips the phone over.
lines: That's a book club. A plant book club.
questions.question: Back when you had a crush: did you tell your friends everything, or keep it secret?

choices.label: Told everyone
reply: Told everyone. Group chat had a whole investigation.
Screenshots, timelines, astrology charts. The works.

choices.label: Kept it secret
reply: Kept it secret. Mysterious. Unbothered.
How?? I can't even keep a secret from my reflection.

A:A: You both told everyone. Your friends knew before you two did.
Somewhere there's a group chat about you and {partner} with 400 unread messages.
Honestly, your friends deserve credit at the wedding.
A:B: You kept it secret. {partner} told literally everyone.
Their group chat has screenshots of you. Analyzed. Color-coded.
Ask to see it. Brace yourself. It's going to be adorable.
B:A: You told everyone. {partner} kept it secret.
Your friends knew everything. Their friends knew nothing.
Ask their friends now. Watch them find out on replay.
B:B: You both kept it secret. Ninja crushes.
Nobody knew? Not even one friend? You and {partner} are spies.
Teach me your ways. My face tells everyone everything.

questions.scene: Twig stares out your window. Fidgets. Stares again.
lines: ...Nice weather. Sorry, that's my default.
questions.question: Nervous small talk go-to: the weather, or random fun facts?

choices.label: The weather
reply: The weather. Iconic. My people.
'Nice weather' has gotten me through every awkward moment ever.

choices.label: Random fun facts
reply: Fun facts. Weird, cute, memorable.
Nothing breaks tension like 'did you know otters hold hands?'

A:A: Weather talk for both of you. My kind of couple.
Lowkey, you and {partner} probably bonded over a suspicious cloud.
Sunny with a chance of love. Sorry. I had to.
A:B: Fun facts for you. {partner} defaults to weather.
You're over here talking wombats. They're commenting on humidity.
Somehow it works. Two nervous systems, one love story.
B:A: Weather for you. {partner} panics in fun facts.
They say 'snails can sleep for three years,' you say 'cloudy today.'
That's a nervous duet. Honestly charming.
B:B: Fun facts for both of you. Nerd romance.
I bet you and {partner} flirted entirely through trivia.
Octopuses have three hearts. Imagine having three hearts for someone.

questions.scene: Twig giggles way too loud at nothing, then slaps a paw over her mouth.
lines: Nervous laugh. Ignore it.
questions.question: Back when your partner had a crush on you, what gave it away?
questions.selfQuestion: Back when you had a crush on your partner, what gave it away?

choices.label: Laughing at every single joke
reply: Laughing at every joke. Even the bad ones. Especially the bad ones.
That's not humor. That's love.

choices.label: 'Accidentally' showing up everywhere
reply: 'Accidentally' everywhere. Coincidence? I think not.
Respect. That takes logistics.

choices.label: Staring, then panicking
reply: Staring, then panicking. That's my whole situation.
Eye contact, then full-body chaos.

A:A: You laughed at every joke, and {partner} clocked it.
They knew their jokes weren't that funny. They noticed.
Laughing at bad puns is a love language. I said what I said.
A:B: You showed up everywhere. {partner} thought it was the laughing.
They have no idea you planned those 'random' meetings.
Tell them. Watch them replay every coincidence. Iconic.
A:C: Staring then panicking for you. {partner} thought it was the laughing.
They missed the staring? How? You were probably so loud about it.
Tell them about the panicked looking-away. They'll melt.
B:A: You laughed at everything. {partner} thought it was your 'coincidences.'
So they noticed your schedule but not your fake laughing? Lucky.
Confess the laughing now. They'll be so smug.
B:B: You kept 'accidentally' showing up, and {partner} knew all along.
Your coincidences had a suspiciously good schedule.
And they still let you think it was smooth. That's love.
B:C: Staring then panicking for you. {partner} remembers you always 'being around.'
They noticed you nearby, but not you looking at them.
Next date: stare, panic, then tell them. Full circle.
C:A: You laughed at everything. {partner} noticed the staring instead.
So you were laughing AND staring. Double obvious.
Honestly you were not subtle at all. I love that for you.
C:B: You showed up everywhere. {partner} remembers the staring.
So they caught your eyes but missed your master plan.
Secret mission: still classified. Nice weather.
C:C: Staring then panicking, and {partner} caught every single one.
They watched you look away so fast you almost fell.
Reassuring, honestly. If you two made it, maybe I can too.

questions.scene: Twig spins once, slips on your rug, and grabs the table to stay up.
lines: I'm a terrible dancer. That was a preview.
questions.question: If your partner had to slow-dance in public, what would happen?
questions.selfQuestion: If you had to slow-dance in public, what would happen?

choices.label: Total smooth operator
reply: Smooth operator? Movie scene unlocked.
Spin, dip, the crowd applauds, I faint.

choices.label: Steps on toes, laughs it off
reply: Steps on toes, laughs it off. The cutest version.
Honestly better than smooth. More real.

A:A: You're smooth, and {partner} already knew.
They've seen the kitchen twirls. They know your secret talent.
Next party, you lead. They hold on and look impressed.
A:B: You'd step on toes. {partner} imagined you gliding.
Their expectations: ballroom. Reality: bumper cars.
Laugh through it. Somehow it'll be even more romantic.
B:A: You'd be smooth. {partner} expected stepped-on toes.
They underestimated you. Surprise twirl incoming.
Dip them dramatically. Watch their face. Report back to me.
B:B: Toes get stepped on, and {partner} already knew.
They've accepted their feet are a sacrifice for love.
Laugh-dancing is the best dancing. Ask anyone. Ask me.

questions.scene: Twig scrolls way up in an old chat, then locks her phone very fast.
lines: I wasn't rereading anything. Phones just scroll by themselves.
questions.question: Does your partner reread old texts from your early dating days?
questions.selfQuestion: Do you reread old texts from your early dating days?

choices.label: Yes, all the time
reply: Yes, all the time. Sentimental queen behavior.
There's probably a screenshot folder labeled with a heart.

choices.label: Never, that's chaos
reply: Never. Lives in the present. So healthy.
Teach me. I've reread one 'haha' from Sage 90 times.

A:A: You reread them all the time, and {partner} knew.
They've caught you smiling at your phone at 1 a.m. They know.
Read your favorite out loud. Watch them cringe and melt.
A:B: You never reread them. {partner} imagined you scrolling and smiling.
They think you're more sentimental than you are. Cute.
Try it once. You'll cringe. You'll smile. Worth it.
B:A: You reread them. {partner} thought you never would.
Secret softie exposed. Your sentimental side has been found.
Send them a screenshot from the very first week. Chaos and love.
B:B: Never, and {partner} knew it.
They know you live in the now. Very zen. Very not me.
Maybe they're secretly the one with the screenshot folder.

questions.scene: Twig scribbles in her notebook, crosses it out, scribbles more, crosses that out too.
lines: I'm writing a poem. For a cloud. A specific cloud.
questions.question: If your partner wrote you a love poem, what would it be like?
questions.selfQuestion: If you wrote your partner a love poem, what would it be like?

choices.label: Deep and dramatic
reply: Deep and dramatic. Tissue warning.
Moonlight, longing, seven stanzas.

choices.label: Funny and full of rhymes
reply: Funny with rhymes. Love that.
'You're my honey, you're so funny.' Classic.

choices.label: Three words long
reply: Three words long. Efficient poet.
Short, sharp, devastating.

A:A: Deep and dramatic, and {partner} expected nothing less.
They already know you'd write three pages about their eyebrows.
Frame it. Read it on every anniversary.
A:B: Funny rhymes for you. {partner} expected drama.
They're ready to cry. You hand them a limerick.
Honestly, laughing is romantic too. Ask any comedian's partner.
A:C: Three words for you. {partner} expected drama.
They were ready for an epic. You drop three words and leave.
B:A: Deep and dramatic for you. {partner} expected silly rhymes.
They're ready to giggle. You hand them seven stanzas of feelings.
They'll be crying by stanza two. Bring tissues.
B:B: Funny rhymes, and {partner} called it.
They're already bracing for 'roses are red, you're my bread.'
Honestly, rhyme-based love is underrated.
B:C: Three words for you. {partner} expected funny rhymes.
They wanted 'moon' and 'June.' You gave them pure sincerity.
Somehow that's even more devastating. In a good way.
C:A: Deep and dramatic for you. {partner} expected three words.
They think you're short and sweet. Surprise, you're a novelist.
Make the last line just three words. Twist ending.
C:B: Funny rhymes for you. {partner} expected three words.
They're expecting a short line. You bring a whole rap.
C:C: They know you'd say everything in a single line.
And it would hit harder than any epic poem. Unfair.

questions.scene: Twig closes her eyes and puckers, then opens them, horrified that you saw.
lines: I was stretching my face. Face yoga. It's a thing!
questions.question: How would your partner react to a surprise kiss?
questions.selfQuestion: How would you react to a surprise kiss?

choices.label: Melts instantly
reply: Melts instantly. A puddle. A soft puddle.
Knees gone. Brain gone. Smile stays.

choices.label: Acts shocked, then kisses back
reply: Fake shock, then kisses back. Main character move.
Dramatic gasp, then romance.

A:A: You'd melt instantly, and {partner} knew.
They know you're a marshmallow pretending to be a person.
Surprise them back sometime. Turnabout is cute.
A:B: You'd act shocked first. {partner} expected you to melt.
They'll think they messed up. Then you kiss back. Twist.
Don't leave them hanging too long. Three seconds max.
B:A: You'd melt. {partner} expected fake shock first.
They're ready for drama. You just turn into soup.
That's even better. Seriously. Nice weather.
B:B: Fake shock then kiss back, and {partner} knew.
They're expecting the gasp. They secretly live for it.
The drama is part of the charm. Never stop.
